definitions.explanation: Used to describe doing something with urgency or speed. The te-form of the verb {急|いそ}ぐ (to hurry), functioning as an adverb.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで{朝|あさ}ごはん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I ate breakfast in a hurry.

examples.japanese: {急|いそ}いで⟦{準備|じゅんび}しない→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れる→乗り遅れる：04621_noriokureru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you don't get ready quickly, you'll miss the train.

notes:
The te-form of ⟦{急|いそ}ぐ→急ぐ：01191_isogu⟧ (to hurry), used adverbially to modify the action that follows. It conveys a sense of urgency — that something is being done faster than usual, often because of time pressure.

USAGE:
Placed before the main verb to indicate the manner of the action. Often used in commands or suggestions when time is short.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急|いそ}いで⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ — to go in a hurry
- {急|いそ}いで⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ — to eat quickly
- {急|いそ}いで⟦{準備|じゅんび}する→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧ — to prepare in a rush
- {急|いそ}いで⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧ — to hurry home

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{慌|あわ}てて→慌てる：01874_awateru⟧ — in a fluster, in a panic; implies more disorganization than {急|いそ}いで
- {大急|おおいそ}ぎ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ — in a great hurry; stronger emphasis on urgency
